author: Stephen Crane
title: The Red Badge of Courage: An Episode of the American Civil War
edition: Wikisource transcription (Index: Red Badge of Courage (1895).djvu) of New York: D. Appleton and Company, 1895 (copyright 1894, 1895). Every selected word was collated against OCR of a dated Appleton scan (Internet Archive redbadgeofcourag00cranrich, 1896 printing, copyright 1895) with Project Gutenberg #73 as a second witness; one Wikisource misreading ('lie' for 'He') was corrected, and the Appleton readings that differ from Gutenberg (e.g. 'wide bank', 'cammand', 'Se he went', 'with a air') were confirmed on the page images. Dialect spellings and apostrophe spacing are retained as printed; HTML presentation removed and whitespace normalized. The library holds the whole novel, Chapters I–XXIV, with their chapter headings. The collation and correction above cover the passages used as school nights. The Grade 10 calendar readings add Chapters X–XIII, collated the same way against the 1896 Appleton scan on 2026-11-18: one reading changed, the Wikisource misreading ‘savin'’ corrected to the printed ‘sayin'’ in Chapter XII. Chapters XIV–XIX were collated the same way for further calendar readings on 2026-11-18; where the 1896 printing differs there (‘had not begun’, Chapter XIV; ‘sometimes’ and ‘burr-like’, Chapter XVI), Wikisource’s scan of the 1895 printing reads ‘had not began’, ‘somtimes’ and ‘burlike’ as transcribed, so these 1895 readings, misprints included, stand and the later printing’s corrections are not adopted. Chapters XX–XXIV were collated the same way on 2026-11-18, every difference decided on the 1896 page and on the 1895 page of Wikisource’s scan: three Wikisource misreadings corrected to the printed page (‘lie’ to ‘He’ and ‘everlastin' of soldiers’ to ‘everlastin' ol' soldiers’, Chapter XXI; ‘upon the held’ to ‘upon the field’, Chapter XXII), while the 1896 printing’s revisions ‘mêlée’, ‘fixes them upon’ and ‘Moreover,’ (Chapter XX) and ‘religion-mad’ (Chapter XXIII) are not adopted, because the 1895 page reads ‘melée’, ‘fixes upon’, ‘Too,’ and ‘religion mad’. Elsewhere the Wikisource transcription is reproduced as transcribed.

rights.basis: Original English novel published in 1895 by D. Appleton and Company, before 1931; its US term has expired as of 2026. The dated scan is marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.

acquisition.method: MediaWiki parse API (action=parse, prop=text|revid) for the Wikisource subpages Chapter 1–24 of Red_Badge_of_Courage_(1895), fetched in the printed order of the main page Red_Badge_of_Courage_(1895): Chapter 1 (revision 7729471); Chapter 2 (revision 7729474); Chapter 3 (revision 7729488); Chapter 4 (revision 7729491); Chapter 5 (revision 7729492); Chapter 6 (revision 7729493); Chapter 7 (revision 7737230); Chapter 8 (revision 7742592); Chapter 9 (revision 7743552); Chapter 10 (revision 7750858); Chapter 11 (revision 7764769); Chapter 12 (revision 7767333); Chapter 13 (revision 7771981); Chapter 14 (revision 7772638); Chapter 15 (revision 7773553); Chapter 16 (revision 7773617); Chapter 17 (revision 7780269); Chapter 18 (revision 7787255); Chapter 19 (revision 7787384); Chapter 20 (revision 7787494); Chapter 21 (revision 7787689); Chapter 22 (revision 7788964); Chapter 23 (revision 7790093); Chapter 24 (revision 7790128); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the twenty-four JSON responses concatenated in that order. Removed the Wikisource header, page-number anchors, licence and other no-export elements; each HTML paragraph, and each run of text set directly in a section, became a paragraph with whitespace (including no-break spaces) collapsed to single spaces and italics dropped to plain text; centred verse with line breaks became stanzas; the centred chapter titles became level-2 headings. The one correction the school nights carry from the edition’s declared collation (‘lie’ to ‘He’) was applied at the same place, and the calendar collations’ corrections (‘savin'’ to ‘sayin'’, Chapter XII; ‘lie’ to ‘He’ and ‘of’ to ‘ol'’, Chapter XXI; ‘held’ to ‘field’, Chapter XXII) likewise.
